about: FoodBlock 1.6: every closed list and grammar in the spec (core.md, modules/ and profiles/), for code to load. Where the spec states a list, it matches this file exactly. Year zero: no older shape is read.
type_note: Any other type name matching grammar.type_name is open: stored and passed on, no authority.

needs.note: order: refs that order blocks by cause (a block's causal past also holds every block it names by counted_to). needs: the blocks a block's authority rests on, by type. A block waits until all it needs are held, and is judged once; a fold reads only blocks whose needs are all in its input.

refs.note: Shared ref keys are these lists plus the verbs and the causal keys. refs.of names the kind an instance belongs to; state.kind is a label.

refs_single_note: These two links hold exactly one id; an array there is `grammar` (core.md, section 1).
statuses_note: A counter-offer is an answer (a promise with refs.answers) whose state carries new terms and no status; it is the one answer without a status.

stop.occurrences: { occurrences: [start times] }: named occurrences of a standing promise

circle.removal_rule: Removing a holder of admit or remove takes at least `needed` different holders of remove, the remover among them, each stopping that same member grant. The member removed never counts among them.
circle.roles_shape: state.roles: [{ name, powers }]; the founder holds the first role; powers are from `powers` and from profile powers

genesis.recovery_note: recovery_key_hash and recovery_reach come together or not at all
genesis.recognised: An actor is judged as a genesis when it has state.public_key_sign or has no refs.author; it is then held to this list alone (bad_genesis), and its signature must open with its own public_key_sign (bad_genesis, never bad_signature).
genesis.optional_note: A genesis may also carry any key field (key_fields) but roles, and name and marks. It needs only `required`.

transfer: one of refs.to_owner, refs.to_holder, refs.to_place, state.count

fields.note: The base fields of the closed types. Every closed type may also carry `every`. A closed block says more only through a schema it names (core.md, section 7). The open types (thing, observe, transform and any new word) list nothing here: their fields are described by the base schemas (spec/schemas), and nothing is refused for them.

key_fields.note: Defined once. A genesis (actor) carries them, a key grant carries them, and a member grant and a circle's actor carry roles. A genesis may carry all but roles (genesis.optional); a field that is not a key field is the type's own (fields).

where.values: decimal strings; radius is an amount in m

shapes.money_note: currency is an ISO 4217 code (grammar.currency) or a currency_unit: issuer an id (grammar.id) whose published schema defines the unit, unit its name, decimals an integer 0 to limits.decimals_max. Money in different currencies is never added or compared by the protocol.
shapes.when_window_note: Any of these, at least one, alone or beside the keys of a range or a relative form; not_before and not_after are times, takes a duration (blocks.md, profiles/tasks.md).

places.note: A shape is read only at a place the protocol gives it, never by a field name deeper in. The places are the fields of a block's state, of its terms and scope, and of each item of its lines and split. A value at a place is read by its own keys, and the fields named in bare hold an object, never a bare value. A map nested under a field is data: nothing in it is read as a shape.

grammar.id_note: A bare id is SHA-256. Any other hash carries its name and a colon (suites, hashes).

grammar_notes.duration: Written without lookahead so every regex engine runs it.
grammar_notes.time: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar instant (no 30 February).
grammar_notes.date: The pattern is the shape; the value must also be a real calendar date.

hashes_note: A hash name a reader knows is the bare SHA-256 and every `prefix` of a hash that a suite in `suites` (not `future`) uses: sm3. sha3-256 is listed for the future suite and is unknown until that suite is fixed in vectors.

suites.about: A suite names a hash, a signature algorithm and an envelope together. A key names its suite in state.suite; left out, std. A block is hashed with the hash of the suite of the key that signed it. A reader refuses an unknown suite (refusals.codes.block.unknown_suite).

passkey.form: r then s (64 bytes), the length of authenticatorData (2 bytes, big-endian), authenticatorData, clientDataJSON
passkey.challenge: base64url, no padding, of SHA-256 of the signed bytes (for a block, its id)

sm.key_note: SM4 takes 16 bytes: the content key is the first 16 of its 32 random bytes and HKDF derives 16 bytes (privacy.md, Envelope).

pq.status: noted, not usable until sizes are fixed in vectors; a signature must still fit limits.block_bytes

messages.public_block_note: suite only when it is not std
messages.proof_note: A signed request carries exactly one of counter (an integer above the highest the node has seen from the signer) or challenge (issued by the node, used once). It carries no time.
messages.push_answer_order: taken: round order, ascending by hash inside a round (blocks arriving as the other half of a sealed block held count as the first round). refused: the same, a block's codes in the order of refusals.codes.block. waiting: ascending by hash, each needs ascending. equivocations: each pair sorted, the list sorted.
messages.signature_note: A node signs an answer, and a signer a request, over the UTF-8 canonical JSON of the object without its `signature` key. A pull answer's `request` is the bare SHA-256 hex of the canonical JSON of the whole signed request, `signature` included. header_signature signs the canonical JSON of `header`. An envelope plaintext is the canonical JSON of the plaintext object.

peers.about: Three peers: micro, edge, node. A micro that acts and an index are variants.
peers.micro_clockless: a micro may leave out at and when on observe, transform and transfer; its edge writes an observe of kind receipt

kinds.about: The state.kind labels the protocol reads. Every other kind is an open label.

optional_profiles.about: Optional. A node that has never heard of a profile still accepts every block in it.

successor_view.input: a successor grant, arrivals on this node, the reader's clock

output.events: the standing event observes, one per witness, sorted
output.cancelled: the event observes the person defeated in time, sorted
output.since: the arrival of the needed-th event, or null
output.fired: true once the reader's clock reaches fires

counted_in.input: a ballot result, a commitment, the named counter
counted_in.output: true when the result is signed by that counter and lists the commitment in counted

output.epoch: the current epoch; 0 is the circle actor's key
output.keys: the encryption keys of the epoch's counted rekeys, sorted

payment-proof.schemes_note: labels; any other label is allowed

legacy.note: Not part of the protocol. No node reads an older shape.

refusals.about: Every refusal is { hash, code, detail }: code from these lists, detail free text for people. block: why a node refuses a block's bytes (final for those bytes), or, for unmet, why it waits. fold: why a fold counts a block for nothing. message: why a node refuses a pull or push. valid runs the checks in `checks` in order and stops at the first check that finds anything; its refusal is every code that check found, one per code, in the order of the block codes below.

block.not_canonical: not in canonical form: key or set order, NFC, null, duplicate keys, a repeat in a set, or not exactly type, state and refs
block.float: a number with a fraction or exponent in signed content
block.integer_range: a whole number outside integers.min..integers.max, or -0
block.grammar: an id, salt, nonce, confidence, role ref, language tag or type name outside its grammar
block.time: a time, date or duration outside its grammar
block.calendar: a time or date in the right shape that is not a real calendar instant
block.shape: an amount, money, price, range, mark, share, split, when, where or reveal without its keys
block.type_name: a type that does not match grammar.type_name
block.size_limit: its canonical body is over limits.block_bytes (a sealed copy's block, once opened)
block.after_limit: refs.after names more than limits.after_heads heads
block.audience: an audience that is neither public nor a sorted list of commitments
block.bad_genesis: a genesis with author, prev, after or seq, not public, missing a genesis field, with only one of the recovery fields, or not signed by its own key
block.chain: a seq or prev that does not fit its key's chain, or a skip that goes backwards
block.at_missing: no at on a block that is not an observe, transform or transfer
block.unmet: the block rests on blocks the checker does not hold (its prev, an offer it answers, a grant it acts under or passes on, a counted_to): not a refusal but a wait; judged once, when they arrive
block.bad_hash: an id sent with it is not the hash of its canonical bytes
block.bad_signature: its signature opens with no key of its author
block.void_key: signed by a key of its author that does not speak for it: void, frozen, or rotated past counted_to
block.unknown_suite: a key that names a suite the reader does not know, or a key, signature or id outside its suite's grammar
block.not_own_rotation: a rotation signed by none of the key it replaces, the recovery key, or the operator of an agent or machine
block.recovery_scope: the recovery key signed something other than a key grant or a defeats a profile gives it
block.required: a closed block missing a required field (core.md, section 7)
block.undeclared_ref: on a closed type, a ref key neither shared nor declared by its schema
block.undeclared_field: on a closed type, a state field neither its type's base field nor declared by its schema
block.status_not_answer: a status on a block that neither answers nor updates its author's own
block.bad_status: a status not in statuses, stopped without a valid stop, or a stop beside any other status or none
block.not_a_side: a promise, or a deal block, signed by neither side, nor the circle it signs as, nor the grantor of the grant it acts under
block.deal_not_named: an answer or counter in a deal that does not name the deal's first promise, exactly, in refs.for
block.lines: a line without an id unique in the promise, a top-level price or quantity beside lines, or refs.what not the lines' what
block.wider_than_parent: a child grant's scope or depth wider than its parent's on any field
block.not_receiver: a grant passed on by someone other than its parent's receiver
block.scope_until: a grant others act under without scope.until, or a key, member or operator grant with one
block.bad_roles: a circle roles list whose powers are not in powers (or a profile's powers), or a founder with no first role

fold.not_a_side: signed by neither side nor an agent under a side's live grant
fold.open_offer_counter: a counter to an open offer: it ends nothing; only the author ends an open offer
fold.not_live: acts under a grant that is not live, or outside its scope, or is an act that moves things or binds someone with no trusted schema saying undo ok and neither a specific accepted ask nor a grant naming it with a limit
fold.no_role: signs as a circle without a role with the sign power, in the circle's fold of its causal past
fold.not_counted: a settling block the receiver has not accepted and no confirmer the grounds name has confirmed
fold.equivocation: one of a pair that name one prev: proof, counted for nothing
fold.quote_only: an accept of a quote request: an agent's ask whose grant does not name the act binds no one

message.bad_signature: the message is not signed by the signer it names
message.replay: its counter is not above the highest seen, or its challenge was not issued or was used
message.not_admitted: the node's admission rule does not admit it
message.not_human: a first block to a stranger signed by an agent, outside the receiver's order channel

identity.input: an id and the blocks held

output.signed_by_author: { hash: true when the block is the id's }
output.frozen: the frozen keys among them, sorted
output.operators: authors of live operator grants naming it, sorted

promise_stage.input: a first promise, or an allocation (promises.md), and the blocks held; no clock. A promise that rests on blocks not held, one that speaks for neither side, or an allocation the open offer does not bind has no stage (null)

output.stage: offered, asked, declined, stopped, accepted, underway, done or reversed
output.offer: the offer the binding accept answers; with none, the live offer when there is only one, else null
output.live: every live offer, sorted (two counters to one offer both stand)
output.accept: the binding accept's hash, or null
output.quantity: the quantity chosen, or null; on an open offer, the sum its allocations bind
output.takers: [{ who, request, allocation, quantity }] on an open offer, in causal order; in an allocation's own deal, that one taker
output.forks: allocations that do not see the one before, or accepts of live offers that do not see each other: sorted, none counted
output.lines: [{ id, needed, moved }], id null without lines
output.total: money the price comes to, or null
output.paid: money counted to the from side, or null

circle_state.input: a circle and the blocks held

output.removed: { id: counted_to or null }: null when the stop names none

may_act_as.input: a block, a circle, a role or none
may_act_as.output: true when the author holds the sign power through a role in the circle's fold of the block's causal past

members_then.input: a block and a circle or circle#role
members_then.output: the member or holder ids, sorted

where_now.output: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known

output.owner: an id, or null after a transfer to an open receiver
output.transfers: the counted ownership transfers, in order
output.conflict: the crossing pair, sorted, or null

chain.input: the blocks of one signing key, and the id of the block that brought that key in
chain.head: hash of the block with the highest seq, or null when two share it
chain.length: the key's blocks that count: both blocks of an equivocation pair and every later block of the key are left out
chain.gaps: seq numbers missing that no skip block explains: the lowest first, at most limits.gaps_max
chain.equivocations: pairs of hashes naming one prev, each pair sorted
chain.broken: hashes whose prev does not name the block before
chain.ok: true when there are no unexplained gaps, equivocations or broken links

next_link.seq: the next seq for the key
next_link.prev: the hash of the key's previous block, or of the block that brought the key in

consent.input: a person, a sender (or none), optionally the hash of the grant the sender's block acts under (refs.under), and the blocks held

output.word: yes, stop, keep or move, or null
output.block: the consent block that decides (the lowest hash of tied blocks that agree), or null

consent.note: The person's own blocks count for every word; anyone else's counts only as a stop that binds the recorder's own side, or as a yes from outside the asker's side that has a stop in its causal past. A stop wins any tie; a tie of other words gives null. There is no public list.

views.about: A view reads a fold and the reader's clock or arrivals, and says whose.

promise_view.input: a first promise, the blocks held, the reader's clock
promise_view.output: the promise_stage answer, with stage expired once the clock passes expires and nothing binds

live_grant.clock: the node that relies on the act, when it takes the block in
live_grant.input: an act block, its grants, that clock
live_grant.output: true when every grant's scope.until is later than the clock

recovery_reach.input: a recovery rotation, the identity fold, the reader's arrivals
recovery_reach.output: the voided blocks the reach protects, sorted

withdrawal_seen.input: a withdrawal, a counterparty block, its node's arrivals
withdrawal_seen.output: true when the withdrawal is in the block's causal past, or the node records any arrival of it (no times are compared)

due.clock: the performer's own, from the anchor's arrival on its node
due.input: a promise with a relative when, the performer's arrivals and clock
due.output: the instant it falls due, or null while the anchor has not arrived

door.about: The door is the one call every implementation answers: an op name and positional arguments (JSON), and a result (JSON). spec/vectors.json `door` holds one or more cases per op below: `args`, then `expect` (a subset match: every key given must match, extra keys in a result do not matter; a list or text must match exactly when the case says `exact`, and lists are compared in order), or `codes` (the refusal codes, in order), or `error`. An implementation conforms when it answers every case. An op outside this table is outside the protocol.

conventions.block: { type, state, refs }: a block as written (core.md, section 1).
conventions.full_block: a block with its `hash` (its id), its `signature` (hex) and, when its key's suite is not std, `suite`: { hash, type, state, refs, signature, suite? }. This is what an op that takes blocks held, a story or a store reads. Order in a list of held blocks never matters.
conventions.id: a hash: 64 lowercase hex (or a hash name and colon first). `time`: the text of core.md, section 3. `arrivals`: an object { hash: time } of when this reader's node took each block in; null or a missing hash means unknown. `clock` or `now`: a time.
conventions.refusals: a list of { code, detail }. A case with `codes` compares the codes only, in the order of protocol.json refusals.codes. Details are free text.
conventions.keys: public keys and signatures are hex as in core.md, section 2; a private key is the seed hex for p256 and sm, and for std the seed, which `keypair` also writes as PKCS#8 DER hex (`302e020100300506032b657004220420` then the 32 seed bytes).
conventions.suite_arg: an optional suite name, default std

args: seed: 64 hex (the 32-byte seed of core.md, section 2)

suite_of_key.result: the suite whose SPKI prefix the key starts with, else null

sign.result: signature hex over the canonical bytes of the block (core.md, section 2: deterministic)

verify.result: true when the signature opens (a passkey signature included); the suite is the key's

hash.result: the id of that block in that suite

valid.result: refusals (core.md, section 8); empty when valid. `held` is the context

args: text: the block as JSON text
strict_text.result: what the bytes alone say, with no context: `not_canonical` for text that breaks canonical.md (a repeated key, a lone surrogate) or is not exactly { type, state, refs }, else the refusal of the first of checks 2, 3 and 4, else of check 8 (core.md, section 8)

refusals.result: refusals of `check` (core.md, section 8): checks 1 to 4 and 8, all codes found

needs.result: the ids the block rests on (protocol.json needs), sorted ascending; with `held`, only those not held

recovery_key_hash.result: identity.md: the suite's hash of the key's SPKI hex as UTF-8 text

wrap.result: the message { version, block, signature, suite? } (core.md, section 6)

unwrap.result: the full block { hash, type, state, refs, signature, suite? }; the id is recomputed

header.result: the public header { author, seq, prev, hash } with `withheld` or `skip` when the block says so (privacy.md)

seal.result: the envelope (privacy.md); `fixed` gives the random values (hex, the ephemeral private key, content key, content nonce, one key nonce per recipient) so a case is exact; with none the values are random

open.result: the plaintext JSON; a recipient it is not for is an error

cbor_encode.result: lowercase hex of the CBOR message [t, block, signature, suite?] (encoding.md); `short` uses key table 1 and t = 1

cbor_decode.result: the full block; the id is recomputed from the canonical JSON

passkey_challenge.result: the WebAuthn challenge for the block: base64url, no padding, of the 32 bytes of SHA-256 of its canonical bytes, which is its id for a std or p256 key (passkeys.md)

verify_message.result: true when `signature` opens over the canonical JSON of the object without `signature` (nodes.md)

key_timeline.result: [{ key, by, signer, void, frozen, suite }]: every key the identity fold knows (identity.md), `by` the block that brought it in

recovery_reach.result: the voided blocks the reach protects (identity.md), sorted

args: last: full_block of the key's chain, or null
next_link.result: { seq, prev }: the next place in the key's chain (core.md, section 5)

args: brought_in: id of the block that brought the key in
check_chain.result: { head, length, gaps, skips, equivocations, broken, ok } (folds.md, chain)

fork_pairs.result: the equivocating pairs, each sorted, the list sorted (nodes.md)

past_of.result: the ids in its causal past (blocks.md), sorted

sees.result: true when `earlier` is in the causal past of `later`

matches.result: true when the block matches the pull filter (nodes.md, Pull)

due.result: the instant it falls due (the anchor's arrival plus `wait`), or null while the anchor has not arrived

promise_stage.result: the promise_stage answer of protocol.json folds (folds.md)

promise_view.result: the same answer, with stage `expired` as folds.md says

live_grant.result: true when every grant's scope.until is later than the clock

may_act_as.result: true or false (folds.md); no code is returned

under_ok.result: true when the block speaks for its grantor under the grant it names (refs.under): the grant is held, is for its signer, is live, covers the act, and an act that moves things or binds is not irreversible, or has what that needs (authority.md); no clock is read

ownership.result: { owner, transfers, conflict } as the fold `ownership` (folds.md)

where_now.result: the places (hashes), sorted; empty when none is known (folds.md)

args: within?: a block, to read the circle as of its causal past
circle_state.result: { founder, members, removed } or null when the circle is not held (folds.md)

args: under?: grant id the sender's block acts under
strangers_today: integer, blocks this node took today from senders not in parties
long?: true for the ten-character form
receipt_code.result: the code of profiles/short-form.md: XXXX-XXXX, or XXXXX-XXXXX when long

args: text: a code as a person types it
code_matches.result: true when the text names the block: case, spaces and hyphens ignored, O read as 0, I and L as 1; eight characters match the short code, ten the long one

deposit_shape_ok.result: true when it has exactly those keys, money a money shape and holder an id

accept.result: { taken: [id], waiting: [{ hash, needs: [id] }], refused: [{ hash, code, detail }], equivocations: [[id, id]] } in the order nodes.md, Push, fixes

args: incoming: [sealed message { version, header, header_signature, envelope? }]
accept_sealed.result: the same shape as `accept`, judged from the public headers (privacy.md)

args: log: [{ n, block, header?, header_signature?, copies? }]
answer_pull.result: { node, request, blocks: [{ n, message }], next, signature } (nodes.md, Pull); `signature` only when a private key is given

convert.result: outside the protocol (legacy/converter.md); a case carries `oracle: false`

merkle_root.result: encoding.md, Large content: the Merkle root (64 hex) over the chunks; an error (argument) for no chunks

merkle_proof.result: the proof of that chunk: the sibling hashes (hex) from the leaf up; an error (argument) for an index that is no chunk

merkle_verify.result: true when the proof shows the chunk is chunk `index` of `count` under the root

base_fields.result: the base fields of that type, beside `every`: the list in `fields`, or none for an open type

cbor.about: Compact form of a public block (encoding.md). The id is always the hash of the canonical JSON; CBOR is transport only. At year zero the key table is reset: this is table 1.

bytes.about: A value at one of these paths that matches its grammar is a byte string; otherwise text (an id with a hash prefix stays text). `[]` is each element, `*` any key. hash: 32 bytes. sign_key: std 32 raw bytes (suites.std.sign_key.spki_prefix put back), other suites the whole SPKI. encrypt_key: the suite's raw bytes. nonce: 16 bytes.

cbor.time: A value at a time field (time_fields, in time_fields_checked_in) matching grammar.time is an integer of milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z; when.from and when.to likewise.

message.header_note: A chain header has exactly the four keys. seq is an integer; the three ids are 32-byte byte strings when bare, text when they carry a hash prefix.
